message: Arabic letter ي, ى, ك or ه: Urdu writes ی (U+06CC) or ے (U+06D2), ک (U+06A9) and ہ (U+06C1), and ھ (U+06BE) only inside an aspirate such as بھ or کھ (STYLE 22.4).
Letter or spelling that Urdu software text does not use (ة ۀ ۓ ە, or the old لئے, کیلئے, کیلیے): write ہ, ہو‌ئے-type words with ئے (ہوئے, گئے) and کے لیے (STYLE 22.4).
ھ (do-chashmi he) outside an aspirate: it belongs only after ب پ ت ٹ ج چ د ڈ ر ڑ ک گ ل م ن (بھی, کھولیں, ٹھیک); write ہ elsewhere (STYLE 22.4).
ASCII full stop at the end of a sentence in Urdu text: write ۔ (U+06D4) attached to the last word; "." stays only inside numbers, versions, file names and code (STYLE 22.3).
ASCII comma, semicolon or question mark after Urdu text or a placeholder: write ، (U+060C), ؛ (U+061B) or ؟ (U+061F) (STYLE 22.3).
ASCII comma after a Latin word or number inside an Urdu sentence: write ، (U+060C); the comma of digit grouping (1,234) stays (STYLE 22.3).
Extended Arabic-Indic or Arabic-Indic digit or separator (۰-۹, ٠-٩, ٪ ٫ ٬): numbers keep 0-9 with the English decimal point and grouping, 1,234,567.5 (PD-OI-106, STYLE 22.3).
Space before ، ؛ ؟ ۔ or the label colon: attach the mark to the word before it and put one space after it (STYLE 22.3).
Straight quotes or guillemets around a cited name: write curly double quotes “…” (U+201C, U+201D), as CLDR ur does; code such as /key="value" keeps its straight quotes (STYLE 22.3).
Space inside “…”: write the quoted text against both marks, “{name}” (STYLE 22.3).

Right arrow → inside an Urdu sentence points against the reading order: write ← (U+2190) or words (سے … تک, پھر); → stays only as a picture of the figure direction (دائیں →) and inside code (STYLE 22.3).
Range, slash or x between two numbers or placeholders: a right-to-left line shows the values reversed; write {start} سے {end} تک, or one word per value (STYLE 22.3).
A hyphen or dash between spaces is not Urdu punctuation: rewrite with ، or : or parentheses (STYLE 22.3).
Diacritic (zabar, zer, pesh, shadda, sukun, khari zabar): Urdu UI text writes none and does not mark the izafat; the only mark allowed is tanween fath on a final alef (فوراً, تقریباً) (STYLE 22.4).
Tatweel (kashida) U+0640: delete it; the Nastaliq face joins the letters itself (STYLE 22.4).
ZWNJ or ZWJ: Urdu compounds in this UI are written with a space (ری سیٹ), and the Nastaliq face joins the letters itself; delete the mark (STYLE 22.4).
Urdu letter glued to a {placeholder}: no suffix, particle or ending touches it; put a class noun beside it (فائل {file}) and write postpositions as separate words ({name} کا) (STYLE 22.5).
Latin letter or digit touching an Urdu letter: put a space between them and no Urdu suffix on a Latin word (GenBank فائل, 5 ریکارڈ) (STYLE 22.4).
Urdu value starting with a Latin word: an element that takes its direction from its text would read left to right; put the Urdu class noun first (فائل GenBank, ٹول LOSAT) (STYLE 22.4).
Not the glossary word: gene and genome are جین and جینوم (وراثہ, موراثہ are coinages), a legend is لیجنڈ (افسانہ and داستان are fiction), a session is سیشن (جلسہ is a meeting) (STYLE 22.1).

Not the glossary word: feature فیچر (not خصوصیت), sequence سیکوئنس (not تسلسل), History سابقات, circular دائروی, linear لکیری, diagram خاکہ, Generate بنائیں, Preview پیش منظر, strand اسٹرینڈ, content مقدار (STYLE 22.1).

Loanword spelling or plural not used here: write اس- (اسٹرینڈ, اسٹیک, اسکیما, اسکور) and keep masculine loanwords unchanged in the plural (5 ریکارڈ, not ریکارڈز); feminine فائل takes فائلیں (STYLE 22.1, 22.5).

Informal or over-formal command or pronoun (کرو, تم, کیجیے): buttons and instructions use the polite plural imperative -یں (کریں, چنیں), help sentences use the passive or آپ with a plural verb (STYLE 22.2).
Three periods or a doubled ellipsis: write one … (U+2026) attached to the last word (STYLE 1.2).
Leading, trailing or doubled space, or an invisible character (NBSP, ZWSP, WJ, BOM): use single ordinary spaces; units keep the source spacing (100 bp) (STYLE 1.2).
Arabic comma before the conjunction یا: Urdu writes no comma before یا between two alternatives.
The other strand is ریورس اسٹرینڈ (glossary row reverse strand), not منفی اسٹرینڈ.
Python follows the Urdu noun in brackets (ریگولر ایکسپریشن (Python)), as the glossary row Python (attributive) writes it.
A Latin option name that starts with a hyphen after an Urdu word is shown with the hyphen on the wrong side (t-): put a Latin word before it (gbdraw -t) or rewrite.
A pair of records takes the oblique plural: ریکارڈوں کی جوڑی / جوڑیاں (STYLE 22.1; as in جینوں کی جوڑی).
A sentence ends on a Latin word before ۔: use another order when one is natural (STYLE 22.4).
اپنے ٹریک محور reads as the compound ٹریک محور (track axis): write their tracks above the axis as اپنے ٹریکوں کو محور کے اوپر.
A count-first label pair or leader pair reads as one compound noun: write the genitive لیبلوں کی {count} جوڑی / لیڈر لائنوں کی {count} جوڑی, as in جینوں کی {count} جوڑی
The plural inputs before a postposition take the oblique ان پٹوں (STYLE 22.1): ان پٹوں کو / کے ساتھ / کا جائزہ; keep ان پٹ for one input or a generic ان پٹ کے طور پر
A possessed noun before کو is oblique, so its genitive is کے: آؤٹ لائن کے رنگ اور چوڑائی کو
کی اجازت سے is with the permission of; larger than X allows is اس حد سے بڑی ہے جس کی X اجازت دیتا ہے
